Vote - Return-Straight-to-Sender - Would you please review the comments carefully and then resubmit whatever you regard as still being viable.

Vote - DEFER - In line 6 ἁρπαγῇ is certainly correct. At the end of line 9 the last upward turn from η probably was the link to a final sigma, like e.g. in τῆς in line 3. The margin of the sheet might have been slightly scaled off, even after the edition, so I would prefer ἐμαυτῆς̣ or ἐμαυτῆ[ς]. In line 21 the new reading is paleographically fine, but I would neither exclude the edition’s one. In any case, the meaning is not evident, so I would suggest the author justify it in an article, rather than proposing it here.
Vote - AcceptText - Accept l. 6 correction; disregard l. 9; l. 21 looks good to me palaeographically

Vote - DEFER - lin6 ἁρπαγῇ is good. lin9 ed.’s ἐμαυτῆς is fine (the foot of eta curls up to form sigma); we would dot the sigma nowadays. lin21 τί σκ̣επτόμενοι is not bad, but where else in the papyri is this verb used in the present (and in this sense)? The aorist forms are common (but usually not in this sense). It needs further comment.
Submit - Corrections in three lines: 6, 9, 21.
Commit - Correction in three lines: l. 6 ἁρπαγαῖς => ἁρπαγῇ; l. 9, there is no final sigma in the word ἐμαυτῆς => ἐμαυτῆ<ς>; l. 21 τίνι ἐπα̣γόμενοι => τί σκ̣επτόμενοι
